candidates.label: Bethlehem
candidates.support: Wikidata's coordinate for the town agrees with the Digital Atlas of the Roman Empire's point to within about 130 meters, and both sit within about 150 meters of the traditional birth site marked by the Church of the Nativity.

summary.text: Bethlehem is a town in the fertile limestone hill country of Judea, less than 10 km (6 miles) south of Jerusalem. A few kilometers to the southeast stood Herodium, the hilltop fortress and palace that Herod the Great built and named after himself, and where he was buried. Bethlehem was already known in the Old Testament as the home town of David, centuries before Matthew and Luke identify it as the birthplace of Jesus.

history.text: Luke's Gospel says that Joseph went up to Bethlehem, "David's city," with Mary to be enrolled under a decree of Caesar Augustus, and that Mary laid her newborn son "in a feeding trough, because there was no room for them in the inn." Luke also describes shepherds "in the same country... keeping watch by night over their flock," who were told that a Savior had been born "in David's city." Matthew describes wise men from the east, led by a star that "stood over where the young child was," and King Herod then killing the boys of Bethlehem and its surroundings who were two years old and under.

By at least the second century, Christians believed that a cave at Bethlehem was the birthplace of Jesus. A church built over the cave was completed in AD 339 under the Roman emperor Constantine and replaced in the mid-sixth century under the Byzantine emperor Justinian; that building, with later changes, still stands, making the site one of the longest continuously venerated places in Christian tradition.

Today Bethlehem is a Palestinian town and, as it has been for some 1,700 years, a pilgrim destination. The Church of the Nativity, a UNESCO World Heritage Site and the oldest Christian church in daily use, stands over the traditional birth cave. A pilgrimage route runs to it from the town's traditional entrance along Star Street to Manger Square.

scripture.textWEB: Now in those days, a decree went out from Caesar Augustus that all the world should be enrolled.
Now when Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judea in the days of King Herod, behold, wise men from the east came to Jerusalem, saying,
They said to him, “In Bethlehem of Judea, for this is written through the prophet,
‘You Bethlehem, land of Judah, are in no way least among the princes of Judah; for out of you shall come a governor who shall shepherd my people, Israel.’”
He sent them to Bethlehem, and said, “Go and search diligently for the young child. When you have found him, bring me word, so that I also may come and worship him.”
They, having heard the king, went their way; and behold, the star, which they saw in the east, went before them until it came and stood over where the young child was.

Then Herod, when he saw that he was mocked by the wise men, was exceedingly angry, and sent out and killed all the male children who were in Bethlehem and in all the surrounding countryside, from two years old and under, according to the exact time which he had learned from the wise men.
Joseph also went up from Galilee, out of the city of Nazareth, into Judea, to David’s city, which is called Bethlehem, because he was of the house and family of David,
She gave birth to her firstborn son. She wrapped him in bands of cloth and laid him in a feeding trough, because there was no room for them in the inn.
There were shepherds in the same country staying in the field, and keeping watch by night over their flock.
For there is born to you today, in David’s city, a Savior, who is Christ the Lord.
When the angels went away from them into the sky, the shepherds said to one another, “Let’s go to Bethlehem, now, and see this thing that has happened, which the Lord has made known to us.”
Hasn’t the Scripture said that the Christ comes of the offspring of David, and from Bethlehem, the village where David was?”

otConnections.note: Micah's prophecy naming Bethlehem Ephrathah as the origin of a future ruler is quoted in Matthew 2:6 as being fulfilled by Jesus' birth there.
Bethlehem is the setting of the book of Ruth and the home of Ruth's descendant David, background for the Davidic association invoked in the Gospel birth narratives.

politicalHistory.entity: Kingdom of Herod the Great (ruler: Herod the Great)
Ethnarchy of Judea, Samaria and Idumea (ruler: Herod Archelaus)
politicalHistory.note: The emperor Augustus did not grant Archelaus the royal title his father's will asked for, only "ethnarch." This area's drawn shape also includes Gaza and the coastal strip north to Rhinocolura; Josephus records that Augustus took Gaza itself, with Gadara and Hippos, from Herod's kingdom at his death and added it to the province of Syria, but since none of these is its own area on this map, Gaza's land and this coastal strip stay within the area around them.

politicalHistory.entity: Roman province of Judea (ruler: Prefects, e.g. Pontius Pilate)
politicalHistory.note: Luke links a census "when Quirinius was governor of Syria" to Jesus' birth, which Luke and Matthew place in Herod's days; the Jewish historian Josephus dates Quirinius's own census of Judea to this year. This map takes no position on how the accounts relate. This area's drawn shape also includes Gaza and the coastal strip north to Rhinocolura, which stayed in the province of Syria from 4 BC on (rule 4, as in the previous period's note).
